key_concepts: [url]Learn to Create and Connect Pipes in Blender^^https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4Lt7Fm7h53U[/url]
Learn how to quickly create and connect pipes in Blender using correct geometry.

content: Select all vertices in the default cube and [k]M,A[/k] to reduce them to a single vertex (Image 1). [k]E,Z[/k], [k]E,X[/k] to extrude it out (Image 2). Select the first vertex and [k]Shift-D,Y[/k] to duplicate it and move it out, and then [k]E,Y[/k] to move it back (make sure Auto Merge is not enabled) (Image 3). These are going to be bends in the pipes, so select the vertex where the bend will go and [k]Ctrl-B,V[/k] and make a bevel with four segments (Image 4).

image.caption: Image 1 - Selecting all vertices in the default cube and merging them to a single vertex
Image 2 - Extruding it out in the z- and x-axes
Image 3 - Selecting the first vertex, duplicating it and moving it out in the y-axis, and then extruding it back with Auto Merge disabled
Image 4 - Selecting the vertex where the bend will go and adding a bevel with four segments

content: [k]Tab[/k] into Object Mode, and [k]Object > Convert > Curve[/k] (Image 5). In the Data Properties tab, under Geometry, update the Bevel Depth to increase the size (Image 6). We will shrink the size of the upper pipe by going into Edit Mode, selecting one if its vertices and pressing [k]Ctrl-L[/k] to get all linked geometry (Image 7). [k]Alt-S[/k] to scale it down so it becomes a small pipe feeding into a larger one (Image 8).

image.caption: Image 5 - Going to Object Mode and converting to a Curve
Image 6 - Updating the Bevel Depth in the Data Properties tab under Geometry to increase the size
Image 7 - Going into Edit Mode, selecting one of the upper pipe's vertices and pressing Ctrl-L to get all linked geometry
Image 8 - Scaling it down so it becomes a small pipe feeding into a larger one

content: [k]Object > Convert > Mesh[/k] to change it back to a mesh (Image 9). [k]P,L[/k] and this will separate the mesh into two objects (Image 10). Select the bottom pipe and add a Boolean Modifier with the other pipe as the Target (Image 11). Apply the modifier, [k]Tab[/k]] into Edit Mode, [k]/[/k] Local View, and you will see the results (Image 12).

image.caption: Image 9 - Converting it back to a mesh
Image 10 - Separating the mesh into two objects
Image 11 - Selecting the bottom pipe and adding a Boolean Modifier with the other pipe as the Target
Image 12 - Applying the modifier, going into Edit Mode and Local View to see the results

content: Select the faces inside the cutout and [k]X,F[/k] to delete them (Image 13). [k]Numpad7[/k] into Top View, [k]K[/k] to activate the Knife Tool, and after [k]LMB[/k], press [k]A,C[/k] to activate Angle Snap and Cut Through (Image 14). Make two cuts through the pipe (Image 15). Move the two edge loops closer to the hole (Image 16) and add a Loop Cut in the middle (Image 17)..

image.caption: Image 13 - Selecting the faces inside the cutout and deleting them
Image 14 - Going to Top View, activating the Knife Tool and enabling Angle Snap and Cut Through
Image 15 - Making two cuts through the pipe
Image 16 - Moving the two edge loops closer to the hole
Image 17 - Adding a Loop Cut in the middle

content: We want to clean up any n-gons we have. Connect the two vertices along the x-axis to the hole (Image 18). Connect this vertex to the inner one next to it (Image 19). Repeat this for the other three (Image 20). [k]J[/k] join the remaining vertices to fix the last n-gons (Image 21).

image.caption: Image 18 - Connecting the two vertices along the x-axis to the hole to clean up n-gons
Image 19 - Connecting this vertex to the inner one next to it
Image 20 - Repeating this for the other three
Image 21 - Joining the remaining vertices to fix the last n-gons

content: [k]A,M,B[/k] to remove any extra vertices. [k]Ctrl-R[/k] to add a Loop Cut, but before placing it, [k]E[/k] to disable Even so that it is closer to the hole (Image 22). Select the inner edge loop and [k]G,Z[/k] to move it up, which will create a smoother transition (Image 23). [k]E,Z[/k], [k]S,Z,0[/k] to extrude some geometry anf flatten it (Image 24). [k]Ctrl-R[/k] to add another Loop Cut with Even disabled (Image 24). [k]Tab[/k] into Object Mode, select the other pipe, and move its bottom edge loop up to create separation (Image 25).

image.caption: Image 22 - Adding a Loop Cut with Even disabled so it is closer to the hole
Image 23 - Selecting the inner edge loop and moving it up in the z-axis to create a smoother transition
Image 24 - Extruding some geometry and flattening it, then adding another Loop Cut with Even disabled
Image 25 - Going to Object Mode, selecting the other pipe, and moving its bottom edge loop up to create separation

content: In Object Mode, select both pipes and [k]Ctrl-J[/k] to connect them (Image 26). In Edit Mode, [k]Ctrl-R[/k] to bring up the Edge Menu and [k]Bridge Edge Loops[/k] to connect them (Image 27). Select one of the edge loops and [k]X,I[/k] to dissolve it (Image 28). [k]RMB > Shade Smooth[/k] and add a Subdivision Surface Modifier to make it smooth (Image 29).

image.caption: Image 26 - Selecting both pipes in Object Mode and joining them
Image 27 - Going into Edit Mode and using Bridge Edge Loops from the Edge Menu to connect them
Image 28 - Selecting one of the edge loops and dissolving it
Image 29 - Shading smooth and adding a Subdivision Surface Modifier to make it smooth

key_concepts: [url]Blender Stylized Trees Tutorial^^https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jNDYp8aqiyw[/url]
Using a geometry node setup to create stylized and painterly trees in Blender!.

content: Start with the default cube, and in Edit Mode with all vertices selected, [k]A[/k] to select all and [k]M,A[/k] to merge them in the center (Image 1). [k]Numpad1[/k] into Front View and [k]E[/k] to extrude the vertices into branching shape (Image 2). [k]Shift-D[/k] to duplicate one of the vertices and branch off in a different direction (Image 3).

image.caption: Image 1 - Starting with the default cube, selecting all vertices in Edit Mode and merging them in the center
Image 2 - Going to Front View and extruding the vertices into a branching shape
Image 3 - Duplicating one of the vertices and branching off in a different direction

content: Move to a different angle and rotate the branches so the tree isn't flat (Image 4). [k]Tab[/k] into Object Mode, [k]Object > Convert > Curve[/k] (Image 5). Go to the Data Properties tab, and under the Geometry section, update the Bevel Depth and Resolution (Image 6).

image.caption: Image 4 - Moving to a different angle and rotating the branches so the tree isn't flat
Image 5 - Going to Object Mode and converting to a Curve
Image 6 - Going to the Data Properties tab and updating the Bevel Depth and Resolution under the Geometry section

content: In Edit Mode, [k]O[/k] for Proportional Editing and then select the vertices you want to adjust and [k]Alt-S[/k] to scale them in (Image 7). Extrude the bottom vertex down and scale out slightly (Image 8).

image.caption: Image 7 - Going into Edit Mode, turning on Proportional Editing, selecting vertices and scaling them in
Image 8 - Extruding the bottom vertex down and scaling out slightly

content: Set the 3D Cursor at the tops of the branches and in Object Mode add an Icosphere to each one, with one cluster larger than the other (Image 9). [k]Ctrl-J[/k] to join the meshes (Image 10).

image.caption: Image 9 - Setting the 3D Cursor at the tops of the branches and adding an Icosphere to each one in Object Mode with one cluster larger than the other
Image 10 - Joining the meshes together

content: Add a Plane to the scene (Image 11). Scale it in to make it narrow (Image 12). Add two Loop Cuts (Image 13). Scale the edge loops to make a leaf shape (Image 14). From the side, move the middle face up to give a bend (Image 15).

image.caption: Image 11 - Adding a Plane to the scene
Image 12 - Scaling it in to make it narrow
Image 13 - Adding two Loop Cuts
Image 14 - Scaling the edge loops to make a leaf shape
Image 15 - Moving the middle face up from the side to give a bend

content: Add another Loop Cut down the middle (Image 16). [k]G,G[/k] to edge slide the vertices up top (Image 17) and at the bottom (Image 18) to improve the shape. Select the bottom vertex and [k]Shift-S,T[/k] to move the 3D Cursor there and then in Object Mode [k]RMB > Set Origin > Origin to 3D Cursor[/k]. Scale the leaf down and [k]Ctrl-A,S[/k] and apply the scale to everything (Image 19).

image.caption: Image 16 - Adding another Loop Cut down the middle
Image 17 - Edge sliding the vertices up top to improve the shape
Image 18 - Edge sliding the vertices at the bottom to improve the shape
Image 19 - Selecting the bottom vertex, moving the 3D Cursor there, setting the origin to the 3D Cursor, scaling the leaf down and applying the scale to everything

content: Select the leaf clusters and open the Geometry Node Editor (Image 20). Add a [k]Mesh to Volume Node[/k] (Image 21). Add a [k]Distribute Points in Volume Node[/k] next (Image 22). Next we want an [k]Instance on Points Node[/k], an [k]Object Info Node[/k], and use the leaf as the instance (Image 23).

image.caption: Image 20 - Selecting the leaf clusters and opening the Geometry Node Editor
Image 21 - Adding a Mesh to Volume Node
Image 22 - Adding a Distribute Points in Volume Node
Image 23 - Adding an Instance on Points Node and an Object Info Node and using the leaf as the instance

content: [url]Geometry Nodes^^/tutorials/Blender/Blender Guru/Geometry Nodes/Part 1[/url]
Add nodes to randomize the rotation and scale, and expose any variables you want to affect in the Modifier Properties (Image 24).

image.caption: Image 24 - Adding nodes to randomize the rotation and scale and exposing any variables to affect in the Modifier Properties

content: With the Ico Sphere still selected, add a green material (Image 25). If you go into Material Preview Mode, you won't see the green material applied to the leaves, instead we need to work around this. Add a [k]Set Material Node[/k] in the Geometry Editor and choose the 'leaf' material what was just created (Image 26). The leaves don't look right since the material is being applied individually using each leaf's normals. We want to use the leaf cluster object's normals. Add a [k]Sample Nearest Face Node[/k] to read from the mesh's face, set its Data Type to Vector, and a [k]Normal Node[/k] to read the normal values (Image 27).

image.caption: Image 25 - Selecting the Ico Sphere and adding a green material
Image 26 - Adding a Set Material Node in the Geometry Editor and choosing the leaf material
Image 27 - Adding a Sample Nearest Face Node set to Vector data type and a Normal Node to read the normal values

content: Connect the Value output to a [k]Store Named Attribute Node[/k] and change its Data Type to Vector and change its attribute name to 'normals' (Image 28). Connect the [k]Instance in Points[/k] to its Geometry input and pass its output to the [k]Set Material Node[/k] (Image 29). Last thing we need to do is pass the 'normals' attribute to our material. Go the Shader Editor and add an [k]Attribute Node[/k] connecting to the Normal input of the [k]Principled BSDF[/k] and make sure the node's Attribute Type is set to Instancer and the attribute name is 'normals' (Image 30).

image.caption: Image 28 - Connecting the Value output to a Store Named Attribute Node, changing its Data Type to Vector and setting the attribute name to 'normals'
Image 29 - Connecting the Instance on Points to its Geometry input and passing its output to the Set Material Node
Image 30 - Going to the Shader Editor and adding an Attribute Node connected to the Normal input of the Principled BSDF with Attribute Type set to Instancer and attribute name set to 'normals'

content: TBD - he uses color ramps to shade his materials, and gives a quick tutorial on light.

key_concepts: [url]Blender Game Assets Tutorial | Polygon Runway^^https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=424SR79NN-g[/url]
Create game assets and optimize the texturing.
[url]Hammer Tutorial in Blender 2.9^^https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0h7JVBJMNiE[/url]
Create a fancy hammer in Blender 2.9.

content: Start with the default cube. [k]S,Shift-X[/k] to scale it in the y- and z-axes (Image 1). Add a Mirror Modifier in the x- and y-axes with clipping enabled, [k]Ctrl-R[/k] to add two Loop Cuts and delete the left and top halves (Image 2). [k]I[/k] to Inset the face on the end, [k]E[/k] to extrude it out, and then [k]S[/k] to scale it in (Image 3). Subdivide the mesh horizontally and vertically with four Loop Cuts (Image 4). Select the edges in each corner and [k]Ctrl-B[/k] to bevel them (Image 5).

image.caption: Image 1 - Starting with the default cube and scaling it in the y- and z-axes
Image 2 - Adding a Mirror Modifier in the x- and y-axes with clipping enabled, adding two Loop Cuts and deleting the left and top halves
Image 3 - Insetting the face on the end, extruding it out, and scaling it in
Image 4 - Subdividing the mesh horizontally and vertically with four Loop Cuts
Image 5 - Selecting the edges in each corner and beveling them

content: We want to make a circular hole in the ends, so add two more Loop Cuts to the mesh (Image 6). Select the four faces on the end and [k]S[/k] to scale them up (Image 7), then [k]RMB,L,C[/k] to use Loop Tools to make it a circle (Image 8). [k]E[/k] to extrude the faces in (Image 9). Add a Bevel Modifier, increase Segments to 2, reduce the Amount, change the Limit Method to Weight (Image 10).

image.caption: Image 6 - Adding two more Loop Cuts to the mesh to make a circular hole in the ends
Image 7 - Selecting the four faces on the end and scaling them up
Image 8 - Using Loop Tools to make it a circle
Image 9 - Extruding the faces in
Image 10 - Adding a Bevel Modifier, increasing Segments to 2, reducing the Amount and changing the Limit Method to Weight

content: Select the eight edge loops at the corners and change their Mean Bevel Weight to 1 (Image 11). Do the same for the edge loops at the end (Image 12). Select the faces on the side, and [k]I,B[/k] to inset the faces and [k]E[/k] to bring them in towards the center slightly (Image 13). If you get cracks at the corners, fix them by selecting the edge loop and setting the Mean Bevel Weight to 1 (Image 14). Select the top two faces, [k]I[/k] to inset them, [k]E[/k] to extrude them and set the Mean Bevel Weight to 1 (Image 15).

image.caption: Image 11 - Selecting the eight edge loops at the corners and changing their Mean Bevel Weight to 1
Image 12 - Doing the same for the edge loops at the end
Image 13 - Selecting the faces on the side, insetting the faces and bringing them in towards the center slightly
Image 14 - Fixing any cracks at the corners by selecting the edge loop and setting the Mean Bevel Weight to 1
Image 15 - Selecting the top two faces, insetting them, extruding them and setting the Mean Bevel Weight to 1

content: Add a Cylinder with 12 vertices to the scene and [k]S,Shift-Z[/k] to scale it in (Image 16). [k]Ctrl-R[/k] to give it 20 Loop Cuts (Image 17). Add a Decimate Modifier and set the Type to Un-Subdivide with 1 Iteration (Image 18). You won't see any changes in Edit Mode, but switch to Object Mode and you will see a spiral (Image 19).

image.caption: Image 16 - Adding a Cylinder with 12 vertices to the scene and scaling it in
Image 17 - Giving it 20 Loop Cuts
Image 18 - Adding a Decimate Modifier and setting the Type to Un-Subdivide with 1 Iteration
Image 19 - Switching to Object Mode to see the spiral

content: Apply the modifier, and in Edit Mode, [k]3[/k] into Face Select Mode, and [k]Shift,Alt,LMB[/k] to select alternating faces (Image 20). [k]Alt-E,F[/k] to extrude them along normals (Image 21). Move the head on top of the handle (Image 22). Add a Cylinder with 12 vertices, scale it down and move it to where the handle connect with the hammer (Image 23). Round out the bottom with a bevel (Image 24).

image.caption: Image 20 - Applying the modifier, going into Face Select Mode in Edit Mode and selecting alternating faces
Image 21 - Extruding them along normals
Image 22 - Moving the head on top of the handle
Image 23 - Adding a Cylinder with 12 vertices, scaling it down and moving it to where the handle connects with the hammer
Image 24 - Rounding out the bottom with a bevel

content: dd a Circle with 12 vertices, move it to the end of the handle and scale it down (Image 25). Extrude it up in the z-axis (Image 26). Select vertices on opposite sides, [k]O[/k] to turn on Proportional Editing and [k]G,Z[/k] to make a curve (Image 27). Add a Solidify Modifier (Image 28). Add a face to the bottom and [k]Ctrl-B[/k] to bevel (Image 29).

image.caption: Image 25 - Adding a Circle with 12 vertices, moving it to the end of the handle and scaling it down
Image 26 - Extruding it up in the z-axis
Image 27 - Selecting vertices on opposite sides, turning on Proportional Editing and moving them in the z-axis to make a curve
Image 28 - Adding a Solidify Modifier
Image 29 - Adding a face to the bottom and beveling it

content: Let's add a leather strap. Select the bottom face and [k]Shift-S,T[/k] to move the 3D Cursor there (Image 30). Add a Plane and scale it down (Image 31). Rotate it slightly so it points out of the cap (Image 32). Select the vertices at the end sticking out and [k]Ctrl-RMB[/k] to create a path for the handle (Image 33). [k]Ctrl-J[/k] and join all pieces (Image 34).

image.caption: Image 30 - Selecting the bottom face and moving the 3D Cursor there to add a leather strap
Image 31 - Adding a Plane and scaling it down
Image 32 - Rotating it slightly so it points out of the cap
Image 33 - Selecting the vertices at the end sticking out and Ctrl-clicking to create a path for the handle
Image 34 - Joining all pieces together

content: Rotate the hammer 180 degrees (Image 35). For the backdrop, add a Plane to the scene, scale it up, extrude one end and bevel the corner (Image 36). Use the Rock Generator to add a rock, decimate it, and put the hammer on top of it (Image 37). Scatter several rocks around the scene (Image 38). Assign materials and render (Image 39).

image.caption: Image 35 - Rotating the hammer 180 degrees
Image 36 - Adding a Plane to the scene for the backdrop, scaling it up, extruding one end and beveling the corner
Image 37 - Using the Rock Generator to add a rock, decimating it and putting the hammer on top of it
Image 38 - Scattering several rocks around the scene
Image 39 - Assigning materials and rendering

key_concepts: [url]Blender Isometric Line Art House Tutorial | Polygon Runway^^https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1RMQSZ13YXU[/url]
Create a simple Roman-style villa with a line art outline
[url]Sci-fi Painted Crates Tutorial in Blender 2.83^^https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z_dfMhIRNn0[/url]

content: Start with a new scene and delete the camera and light. [k]Tab[/k] into Edit Mode and [k]Ctrl-R[/k] to add a horizontal Loop Cut. Move it towards the top of the cube (Image 1). With the Loop Cut selected, [k]Ctrl-B[/k] to bevel the edge. Then, [k]Alt-E,F[/k] to extrude the edges along their face normals. We will want to extrude them in (Image 2). Add another hortizontal Loop Cut towards the bottom. [k]3[/k] into Face Mode and select the top and bottom faces. [k]S,Shift-Z[/k] and scale those faces in (Image 3).

image.caption: Image 1 - Adding a Loop Cut
Image 2 - Extruding in the bevel
Image 3 - Scaling in the top and bottom

content: Select the front face on the beveled separation between top and bottom. [k]Shift-S,T[/k] to move the 3D Cursor there. Still in Edit Mode, [k]Shift-A[/k] and add a cube. Doing this in Edit Mode will make it part of the same mesh. Scale it down until it is the right shape and size for a locking mechanism (Image 4). Add a Loop Cut across the cube so that we can adjust the front face without changing the back too much (Image 5). Select the front face and [k]S[/k] to scale it in, [k]I[/k] to add an Inset, and then [k]E[/k] to extrude that inwards (Image 6). If you wanted to scale up or down the lock, selecting one of the lock faces and [k]L[/k] would select only faces attached to the lock.

image.caption: Image 4 - Adding a Cube for the lock
Image 5 - Adding a Loop Cut
Image 6 - Extruding in the lock

content: Still in Edit Mode, check the faces to see if there is any z-fighting, and also make sure all faces are oriented correctly. [k]A[/k] to select all topology, and then [k]U,S[/k] to bring up the Smart UV Project dialog. Set the Island Margin to 0.02 and click OK. Go into UV Editing Workspace to see how Blender did (Image 7).

image.caption: Image 7 - Reviewing the unwrapping

content: Go to the Texture Paint Workspace. In the UV side of the screen, click New to create a new Image Texture (Image 8). Give the new image a name, and set its size to 2048x2048 to make it a 2K image (Image 9). Now we want to apply that image. In the Texture Paint side of the screen, click the Texture Slots dropdown and click the button to browse for existing images (Image 10). Apply the image that was just created.

image.caption: Image 8 - Creating a new Image Texture
Image 9 - Setting the texture size
Image 10 - Assigning the texture to the mesh

content: Let's paint the bottom of the mesh blue. Choose a deep blue color for the mesh; you can do this from the color swatch at the top or from the Brush Setting menu on the right. Click the Fill Button from the menu on the right, or press [k]Shift-Space,5[/k]. Click the mesh to fill it with the blue (Image 11). You'll see this reflected not only on the mesh but in the UV Texture Image. Now let's make the top red. [k]Tab[/k] into Edit Mode, [k]3[/k] for Face Selection, and select the top face. [k]Ctrl-Numpad+[/k] to select the adjoining faces (do it twice). [k]Tab[/k] back into Texture Paint mode, and click the button for Paint Mask (Image 12). This will make only the selected faces active for painting. Switch to a deep red color and fill the top faces (Image 13).

image.caption: Image 11 - Filling the texture with blue
Image 12 - The Paint Mask button
Image 13 - Filling the top with a base red color

content: We want to draw some scuff marks on the crates, especially around the edges. Click the Draw button in the Texture Paint view, or [k]Shift-Spacebar,1[/k]. Open the colorpicker and click the eyedropper or [k]Shift-X[/k] and sample the color from the top or bottom. We want use this color, but a less saturated version of it to add scuff marks at the edges. [k]Tab[/k] into Edit Mode, and select one face to start with and then [k]Tab[/k] back into TexturePaint Mode. [k]F[/k] will allow you to enlarge/shrink the radius of the drawing brush, and [k]Shift-F[/k] will let you modify the strength. Play around with different results. If you start drawing on the face and nothing happens, your model may have been accidentally assigned a different texture. Go into the Texture section of the Tool Menu, and clear out any texture that was set (Image 14).

image.caption: Image 14 - Clear any textures that were set
Image 12 - The Paint Mask button
Image 13 - Filling the top with a base red color

key_concepts: [url]Blender Animated Game-Ready Asset Tutorial | Polygon Runway^^https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uA0bUJvc6OQ[/url]
Model and animate a sci fi-  themed vehicle for export to game engines.
[url]Full Blender Tutorial - Textured Medieval House^^https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r99qAsXs4nI[/url]

content: Open a new scene in Blender [k]Ctrl-N,G[/k]. [k]Delete[/k] the Camera, and Light. In Edit Mode, select the Cube and [k]G,Z,1[/k] to move it 1m up, above the origin (Image 1). Change the Transform Pivot Point to 3D Cursor (Image 2) and [k]S,4[/k] to scale the cube up (Image 3). Change the Transform Pivot Point back to Median Point (Image 4). [k]Tab[/k] into Edit Mode and select the top face. [k]G,Z,-1[/k] to move it down a little (Image 5).

image.caption: Image 1 - Opening a new scene, deleting the Camera and Light, going into Edit Mode and moving the Cube 1m up above the origin
Image 2 - Changing the Transform Pivot Point to 3D Cursor
Image 3 - Scaling the cube up
Image 4 - Changing the Transform Pivot Point back to Median Point
Image 5 - Going into Edit Mode, selecting the top face and moving it down a little

content: In Edge Mode, select the front and back edges and [k]RMB,S[/k] to subdivide them (Image 6). Select the new edge and [k]G,Z[/k] to form the roof (Image 7). [k]1[/k] into Vertex Mode and select the opposite vertices in the front and back faces and [k]J[/k] to join them (Image 8).

image.caption: Image 6 - Going into Edge Mode, selecting the front and back edges and subdividing them
Image 7 - Selecting the new edge and moving it in the z-axis to form the roof
Image 8 - Going into Vertex Mode, selecting the opposite vertices in the front and back faces and joining them

content: Go into Face Mode and delete the bottom face (Image 9). Move around the the top and select the faces of the roof. [k]P,S[/k] to separate those pieces and rename them in the Scene Collection (Image 10). Repeat this for the gables (Image 11).

image.caption: Image 9 - Going into Face Mode and deleting the bottom face
Image 10 - Moving to the top, selecting the faces of the roof, separating those pieces and renaming them in the Scene Collection
Image 11 - Repeating this for the gables

content: [k]Ctrl-R,Enter,Enter[/k] to add a vertical Loop Cut under the gable (Image 12). [k]Ctrl-B[/k] to add a bevel for the door (Image 13). Add two more Loop Cuts, one towards the roof, another in the middle (Image 14). Rotate to the side and add a vertical Loop Cut down the middle (Image 15). Bevel this edge as well; this will be the window (Image 16).

image.caption: Image 12 - Adding a vertical Loop Cut under the gable
Image 13 - Adding a bevel for the door
Image 14 - Adding two more Loop Cuts, one towards the roof and another in the middle
Image 15 - Rotating to the side and adding a vertical Loop Cut down the middle
Image 16 - Beveling this edge as well for the window

content: Select the door and window faces and [k]Alt-E,F[/k] to extrude the faces along their normals and move them in (Image 17). Select the face at the bottom of the door frame and [k]X,F[/k] to delete it (Image 18).

image.caption: Image 17 - Selecting the door and window faces and extruding them along their normals and moving them in
Image 18 - Selecting the face at the bottom of the door frame and deleting it

content: Go to Object Mode to select the gable mesh, and in Edit Mode, delete one of the faces. Add a Mirror Modifier in the y-axis to add the opposite side to the scene. Repeat for the roof mesh, mirroring in the x-axis (Image 19). Make sure to enable clipping for both modifiers. Still in Edit Mode with the roof, add a Loop Cut and Bevel it to create the ridges on the side of the roof (Image 20). [k]Alt,LMB[/k] the bottom edge to select all edges and [k]G,G[/k] and hold down [k]Alt[/k] to extrude the roof down to create an overhang (Image 21). Select the middle face of the roof and [k]P,S[/k] to separate it into a new mesh (Image 22).

image.caption: Image 19 - Going to Object Mode, selecting the gable mesh, deleting one face in Edit Mode, adding a Mirror Modifier in the y-axis, and repeating for the roof mesh mirroring in the x-axis
Image 20 - Adding a Loop Cut and beveling it to create the ridges on the side of the roof
Image 21 - Selecting all bottom edges and extruding the roof down to create an overhang
Image 22 - Selecting the middle face of the roof and separating it into a new mesh

content: Select the two outside edges of the roof and [k]S,Y[/k] to scale them out (Image 23). [k]A[/k] to select all faces and [k]Alt-E,F[/k] to extrude the out along normals to raise them outwards (Image 24). Select the underneath face and [k]Alt-S[/k] to bring the bottom side down (Image 25). If you want to even it out, select the bottom edge and then top edge [k]G,G[/k] to Edge Slide them towards the opposite edge (Image 26). Delete the vertices on the opposite side and update Mirror Modifier to include the y-axis.

image.caption: Image 19 - Scaling the roof out along the y-axis
Image 24 - Raising the ridges
Image 21 - Bringing down the opposite face
Image 26 - Sliding the edge to make the beam more even

content: Back in Object Mode select the roof and go into Edit Mode. Select the bottom edge and [k]G,G[/k] to Edge Slide it up to give some space for the beams on the side (Image 27).

image.caption: Image 27 - Sliding the roof up

content: Go into Object Mode and select the house mesh. [k]Tab[/k], [k]1[/k] to go into Edit Mode, Vertex Selection Mode. Select a vertex on one of the bottom corners, and [k]Shift-S,T[/k] to move the 3D Cursor there (Image 28). [k]Tab[/k] into Object Mode and [k]Shift-A > Mesh > Plane[/k] to add a Plane at that spot (Image 29). [k]S[/k] to scale it down (Image 30). [k]G,Shift-Z[/k] to move it in somewhat so it's not too thick; use the dialog to make sure the movement is uniform (Image 31).

image.caption: Image 28 - Positioning the 3D Cursor at the corner of the house
Image 28 - Adding a Plane
Image 28 - Scaling the Plane
Image 31 - Moving the Plane towards the center of the house

content: In Edit Mode [k]E[/k] to extrude the beam up (Image 32). [k]Numpad1[/k] into Front View and [k]Alt-Z[/k] for X-Ray Mode. Select the top vertices and [k]Shift-Ctrl-Alt-S,Y[/k] to skew the top (Image 33) and then [k]G,Z[/k] to move it down (Image 34). [k]Numpad3[/k] into Side View and [k]G,Y[/k] to line it up with the roof beams from the side (Image 35). Finally, add a Mirror Modifier using the house mesh as the Mirror Object, in x- and y-axes (Image 36).

image.caption: Image 32 - Extruding the beam up.
Image 33 - Skewing the top of the beam
Image 34 - Moving the beam down below the roof beams
Image 35 - Lining up the beams from the side
Image 36 - Adding a Mirror Modifier

content: Select the house mesh again, and this time select the edge at the top above the door, and [k]Shift-S,T[/k] to set the 3D Cursor there (Image 37). Again add a Plane, scale it down and [k]R,X,90[/k] to rotate it (Image 38). Scale it along the x-axis and then extrude it out in the y-axis(Image 39). Finish it off with a Mirror Modifier in the y-axis (Image 40).

image.caption: Image 37 - Positioning the 3D Cursor above the door
Image 28 - Adding a Plane for the beam and scaling and rotating
Image 39 - Scaling the Plane in the x-axis and extruding in the y-axis
Image 40 - Adding a Mirror Modifier in the y-axis

content: Select the house mesh and go into Edit Mode. [k]3[/k] into Face Mode and [k]Alt-LMB[/k] to select the bottom face loop (Image 41). [k]Shift-D,LMB[/k] to duplicate in plance and [k]P,S[/k] to separate the selection (Image 42). [k]Tab[/k] back into Object Mode and select the foundation mesh. Go into Edit Mode, Face Mode, and select the three faces by the door and [k]X,F[/k] to delete them (Image 43). [k]2[/k] into Edge Mode, select the top edge loop and [k]G,Z[/k] to move it down (Image 44).

image.caption: Image 41 - Selecting the bottom Face Loop
Image 42 - Duplicating and separating the bottom Face Loop
Image 43 - Deleting the faces by the door
Image 44 - Lowering the top edge

content: Rotate around to the back and [k]Ctrl-R[/k] to add some Loop Cuts (Image 45). Do the same in the front (Image 46). [k]A[/k] to select all vertices and [k]Alt-E,F,S[/k] to extrude the faces out along normals (the [k]S[/k] does it at even scaling) (Image 47). Select the top edge loop and [k]G,Z[/k] to bring it down (Image 48).

image.caption: Image 45 - Adding topology to the rear using Loop Cuts
Image 46 - Adding topology to the front using Loop Cuts
Image 47 - Extruding the faces out at even scaling
Image 48 - Bringing the top Edge Loop down

content: Go around the mesh and [k]G,Z[/k] to move some edges up to create some variation (Image 49). Rotate around to the bottom and delete the bottom faces that won't be seen (Image 50).

image.caption: Image 49 - Adding variation
Image 50 - Deleting the bottom faces.
Image 47 - Extruding the faces out at even scaling
Image 48 - Bringing the top Edge Loop down

content: Select the house mesh and go into Edit Mode. [k]3[/k] into Face Mode and [k]Alt-LMB[/k] to select the faces for the door frame, [k]Shift-D,LMB[/k] to duplicate in place and [k]P,S[/k] to separate the selection (Image 51). [k]Tab[/k] back into Object Mode and select the door frame mesh. Go into Edit Mode,select all faces and [k]Alt-E,F,S[/k] to extrude them inwards by scale (Image 52). Select the faces in front and [k]E,Y[/k] to extrude them out (Image 53). In Edge Mode, select the inner edges at the front and [k]Shift-D,LMB[/k] and [k]P,S[/k] to separate just the edges (Image 54). Go into Edit Mode with that mesh, [k]A[/k] to select all edges and [k]F[/k] to fill it to create the door. Finish by [k]G,Y[/k] moving it back (Image 55).

image.caption: Image 51 - Duplicating a separating faces for the door frame
Image 52 - Extruding the door frame inwards
Image 53 - Extruding the door frame out along the y-axis
Image 54 - Separating the inner edge to make the door
Image 55 - Filling the door and moving it in
